The present technology can be applied to a portion of an image sensor, in which AD conversion is performed.

outputs.L2:
This technology concerns a conversion device, an imaging device, an electronic device, and a conversion technique that can make the circuit configuration smaller.  

The conversion device is provided with a comparator that compares the voltage of an input signal with a ramp voltage of a ramp signal whose level changes over time, and a memory section that stores a code value at the moment when the output of the comparator changes state. This storing operation is carried out multiple times, thereby producing a digital signal with a specified number of bits.  

The specified number of bits is separated into upper bits and lower bits. The lower bits are obtained before the upper bits, and the obtained lower bits are then combined with the upper bits to form the digital signal having the specified bit length.  

This technology may be used in a part of an image sensor where analog-to-digital conversion is performed.
outputs.L3:
The technology relates to conversion apparatuses, imaging apparatuses, electronic apparatuses, and associated methods that are capable of reducing circuit scale while performing analog-to-digital conversion.

In one example, a conversion apparatus compares the voltage of an input signal with a ramp voltage that changes over time. The comparison result changes, or is inverted, when the ramp voltage reaches a level corresponding to the input signal voltage. A storage unit repeatedly holds or captures a code value at the timing when this inversion of the comparison result occurs. By doing so, the apparatus generates a digital signal having a predetermined number of bits that represents the input signal voltage.

The predetermined number of bits is divided into high-order bits and low-order bits. In this configuration, the low-order bits are acquired before the high-order bits. After both portions have been obtained, the low-order bits and the high-order bits are combined to form the final digital signal corresponding to the input signal.

This approach makes it possible to perform analog-to-digital conversion with a reduced circuit scale, because the digital value is generated through divided acquisition and storage of code values rather than by requiring a larger circuit structure for all bits at once. The technology is particularly suitable for application to AD conversion in image sensors, and may be used in imaging apparatuses and other electronic devices that process analog signals and convert them into digital data.
outputs.L4:
The disclosed technology relates to an analog-to-digital conversion technique suitable for imaging devices, image sensors, and other electronic apparatuses that require many compact conversion circuits arranged in parallel. In such systems, reducing the circuit scale of each converter is important because a large number of pixels or signal lines may require individual or column-parallel analog-to-digital converters. The technology achieves this reduction by using a ramp-type conversion method in which an input voltage is compared with a ramp voltage that changes with time.

In operation, a comparison circuit compares the analog input voltage with the time-varying ramp voltage and outputs a comparison result indicating which voltage is larger. As the ramp voltage changes, the comparison result eventually inverts when the ramp voltage crosses the level of the input voltage. A counter or code generation circuit produces code values corresponding to the timing of the ramp voltage. When the comparison result inverts, the current code value is stored. By repeatedly storing code values at inversion timings, the apparatus can determine a digital value corresponding to the analog input voltage.

A notable feature of the technology is the order in which the digital information is acquired. Instead of first obtaining the high-order bits and then the low-order bits, the converter acquires low-order bits before acquiring high-order bits. The low-order-bit information and high-order-bit information are then combined to generate the final digital signal representing the input voltage. This approach allows part of the conversion operation to be simplified and enables the circuitry required for code storage and processing to be reduced.

Because the conversion circuit can be made smaller, the technology is particularly advantageous for solid-state imaging devices such as CMOS image sensors, where many analog-to-digital converters may be integrated on the same chip. By reducing the size and complexity of each converter, the apparatus can improve integration density, lower power consumption, and maintain efficient high-resolution signal conversion. The resulting digital signal can then be used for image processing or for output to subsequent electronic circuits in cameras, mobile devices, machine vision systems, and other imaging or electronic equipment.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called the definite article, and it helps us talk about something specific. For example, when we say “a book,” we could mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we are referring to a particular book that the listener or reader can identify.

This tiny word gives clarity and precision to sentences. It helps connect ideas, point to familiar objects, and guide the reader’s understanding. Without “the,” English would sound less natural and often less clear. Phrases like “the sun,” “the world,” and “the future” show how this simple word can introduce ideas that are unique, shared, or important.

Although “the” may seem ordinary, it is essential. It reminds us that even the smallest words can have great value in language.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an invention involving an AD conversion apparatus in an image sensor that compares an input voltage with a time-varying ramp signal and stores code values when the comparison result inverts.
counterfactuals.output: An analog-to-digital conversion apparatus for an image sensor includes a comparator configured to compare an input voltage corresponding to a pixel signal with a time-varying ramp signal, a counter configured to generate a code value in synchronization with variation of the ramp signal, and a storage circuit configured to store the code value in response to inversion of an output of the comparator. The apparatus may further include a control circuit that controls a timing at which the stored code value is read out and/or resets the comparator and storage circuit for a subsequent conversion operation. By latching the code value at a timing corresponding to a crossing point between the input voltage and the ramp signal, the apparatus converts the pixel signal into a digital value. The configuration enables column-parallel analog-to-digital conversion in an image sensor, improving conversion accuracy and reducing circuit complexity and power consumption.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise technical summary of a conversion apparatus, imaging apparatus, electronic apparatus, and conversion method that reduce circuit scale by acquiring low-order bits before high-order bits during analog-to-digital conversion.
counterfactuals.output:
A conversion apparatus performs analog-to-digital conversion by determining lower-order bits of a digital value before determining higher-order bits. The apparatus includes a comparison circuit, a control circuit, and a digital output circuit. During conversion, the control circuit first executes a low-order-bit acquisition operation for an input analog signal, then executes a high-order-bit acquisition operation based on the result. By reversing the conventional bit acquisition order, the apparatus can simplify reference generation, comparison control, and storage circuitry, thereby reducing circuit scale and power consumption.

An imaging apparatus includes a pixel array that outputs analog pixel signals and the above conversion apparatus that converts the pixel signals into digital pixel data. Because the conversion apparatus has a reduced circuit scale, the imaging apparatus can achieve higher integration density, lower power consumption, and improved suitability for column-parallel or pixel-parallel analog-to-digital conversion architectures.

An electronic apparatus includes the imaging apparatus and a processing unit that processes the digital pixel data. The reduced-size conversion circuitry enables compact implementation of cameras, mobile devices, sensors, and other electronic systems while maintaining required conversion accuracy.

A conversion method includes acquiring low-order bits of a digital conversion result from an analog input signal, subsequently acquiring high-order bits using the low-order-bit result, and outputting a digital signal composed of the acquired bits. This conversion sequence reduces the amount of circuitry required for bit decision and reference control compared with methods that acquire high-order bits first.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

本技術は、アナログデジタル変換装置、固体撮像装置、電子機器、およびアナログデジタル変換方法に関し、特に、画素から出力されるアナログ信号を高精度かつ高速にデジタル信号へ変換することが可能なアナログデジタル変換装置等に関する。

本技術の一態様に係るアナログデジタル変換装置は、時間の経過に応じて電圧値が変化するランプ電圧と、画素信号に基づく入力電圧とを比較する比較部と、比較部の比較結果に基づいてコードを保持する記憶部とを備える。記憶部は、比較部の出力が反転するタイミングに対応するコードを保持するように構成される。また、記憶部は、同一のアナログデジタル変換期間内、または複数の変換動作において、所定のコードを繰り返し保持可能に構成される。

本技術では、ランプ電圧を用いたアナログデジタル変換において、入力電圧に対応する高次側のビットと低次側のビットとをそれぞれ取得し、取得された高次ビットおよび低次ビットを組み合わせることにより、画素信号に対応するデジタル値を生成する。例えば、比較部は、画素信号とランプ電圧との大小関係に応じて比較結果を出力し、記憶部は、当該比較結果の変化に応じてカウンタ値またはコード値を保持する。保持されたコードのうち一部を高次ビットとして用い、他の一部を低次ビットとして用いることで、最終的なデジタル出力コードが形成される。

これにより、ランプ電圧を用いるＡＤ変換方式において、変換時間の増大を抑制しつつ、分解能の向上およびノイズの低減を図ることができる。また、記憶部においてコードを繰り返し保持する構成により、比較結果のばらつきやタイミング誤差の影響を低減し、画像センサにおける列並列ＡＤ変換の精度を向上させることが可能となる。

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an abstract for a patent on a ramp-type analog-to-digital converter where a storage unit repeatedly captures code values at comparator inversion timings to form a digital signal with a predetermined number of bits.
counterfactuals.output: A ramp-type analog-to-digital converter includes a ramp signal generation circuit configured to generate a ramp signal, a comparator configured to compare the ramp signal with an input analog signal and output a comparison signal that inverts when the ramp signal reaches a level corresponding to the input analog signal, a counter configured to generate sequential code values in synchronization with the ramp signal, and a storage unit configured to capture and store code values at inversion timings of the comparison signal. The storage unit repeatedly captures the code values over a plurality of comparison operations and combines or selects the captured code values to form a digital signal having a predetermined number of bits. By acquiring code values at multiple comparator inversion timings, the converter can generate a high-resolution digital output while reducing circuit complexity and improving conversion accuracy in a ramp-type analog-to-digital conversion operation.
